# LegatorOCR v0.2.0-pre.48 (pre-release)

Found by running 18 scanned 1977 newspaper and magazine PDFs (Scînteia, Scînteia Tineretului, Sportul, Flacăra, România literară, Revista economică; 138 pages) through the program, plus two wishes from the tester. Written and tried by the author's assistant on one Linux machine; the automated tests pass on CI runners. **Nothing was tried by hand on Windows, macOS or arm64.**

**Fixed**
- **Scanned-newspaper PDFs (MRC: text in a stencil mask over colour layers) came out without text.** The page was built without the mask, so the text turned into dark smears and the OCR read 40 words from 6 pages. The mask is now applied: the same 6 pages give 19,532 words (the PDF's own text layer has 19,314).
- **Those PDFs were reported as 150 dpi** (the colour layer) instead of 300 dpi (the text mask), so clean-up and OCR were tuned for half the real resolution. On a small magazine page this alone moved the agreement with the existing text layer from 77% to 89%; on newspaper pages it changed little (±0.5 points).
- **The built-in OCR dropped whole pages of very tight columns.** On 3 of 138 pages it read only 25% of the text (the page was thrown away as a picture); it now cuts at the gutters that headlines, picture edges or dust bridge, and reads about 99% of the words of the existing text layer on two of them (1,293 → 5,164 and 1,365 → 4,939 words) and 76% on the third, a small magazine page that gave 0 words before. Of 8 pages that were already read, 7 are unchanged and 1 gained 3 words.
- **The quality report no longer assumes every page is A4** when the file states its resolution (a newspaper sheet is not A4).

**New**
- **Find text… (File menu, Ctrl+F).** Looks for a word such as "Voyager" in the text layer of the project's PDFs or of a folder, lists file, page and line, and a click goes to that page. Ignores diacritics, finds words broken at a line end, can match the old Romanian spelling (1953–1993). Scans without a text layer are counted and need OCR first. The command line already had `--search`.
- **Faster previews after a setting change.** The decoded picture of the last 3 pages stays in memory (up to about 330 MB), so moving a slider no longer decodes a large PDF page again. Not measured on a stopwatch in the window.

**Verified**: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, 858 tests; the OCR agreement figures above are against the PDFs' existing (ABBYY) text layer, which is a cross-check and not ground truth. **Not verified**: speed-up of the preview in the window; Find text on Windows/macOS; Windows, macOS, arm64. On the macOS Intel runner (experimental) two PKCS#12 tests fail because of its OpenSSL, unrelated.
